– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the failing test does:
  DetectCompressorTestCase.testDetection() calls getStreamFor(...) for several sample files. The last one is "bla.tar.deflatez", which is a deflate-compressed file with a zlib header. getStreamFor wraps the file in a BufferedInputStream and passes it to CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream(...) to auto-detect and return the appropriate CompressorInputStream.

- How detection works in the current implementation:
  CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream(InputStream) reads up to 12 bytes as a signature and then checks them against known formats in order: BZip2, Gzip, Pack200, FramedSnappy, Z (Unix “compress”), XZ, and LZMA. If none match, it throws CompressorException("No Compressor found for the stream signature.").

- What’s missing:
  There is no detection for deflate streams in CompressorStreamFactory at all—neither raw deflate nor deflate-with-zlib-header. Consequently, when given a zlib-wrapped deflate file like bla.tar.deflatez, none of the existing checks match and the factory throws the “No Compressor found...” exception, causing the test to fail.

- Why simply constructing DeflateCompressorInputStream by default wouldn’t help:
  DeflateCompressorInputStream has two constructors. The no-args-parameters constructor delegates to the parameters-based one, which creates a java.util.zip.Inflater with nowrap set to the inverse of DeflateParameters.withZlibHeader(). The default DeflateParameters results in nowrap=true (expecting raw/“headerless” deflate). Therefore, even if the factory did try to create a deflate stream by default, it would expect a headerless stream and would fail to read zlib-wrapped deflate unless parameters.withZlibHeader was set to true.

- How this matches the bug report:
  The report states that deflate streams with a zlib header are not detected by CompressorStreamFactory and cause a “No Compressor found...” exception, exactly what happens here. The test uses bla.tar.deflatez to reproduce this behavior.

- Root cause:
  CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream lacks detection logic for deflate with a zlib header and does not create DeflateCompressorInputStream configured for zlib headers. The factory should recognize zlib headers (e.g., CMF/FLG where CM=8 and (CMF<<8|FLG) % 31 == 0) and instantiate DeflateCompressorInputStream with DeflateParameters.setWithZlibHeader(true).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
